title: HIT PARADE
short_description: HIT PARADE - a 3D ring fighting game staged as a late-night TV fight show. Sidestep and circle your opponent inside five 360-degree arenas, with twelve contestants, an arcade season that ends against the host himself, local and online versus, and a full training room.
description:
LIVE ON KNOCKOUT 13.

Every Friday night an underground network takes over the airwaves with HIT PARADE, a no-rules fight show shot on condemned sets across a rotting city. Contestants sign up for money, revenge or fame. The cameras never cut away.

HIT PARADE is a 3D arena fighting game. The two fighters face each other inside a round or eight-sided ring that you can walk all the way around: tap STEP to sidestep off the attack line, hold it to circle-walk around your opponent, and the camera orbits with you. Straight attacks and straight projectiles can be sidestepped on a read (big bodies step less well than small ones); homing attacks (sweeps, spins, wide hooks) track a stepper, and every contestant has homing tools. The ring wall is a weapon too: launch someone into it for a wall splat. Underneath it is classic versus fighting: walk, dash, jump, crouch, block by holding back, light, medium and heavy attacks plus a special button, throws, parries, IMPACT attacks, supers, step-attacks and a cinematic Level 3 super for every contestant.

THE CAST - twelve fighters:
- JOHNNY RIOT, the headliner boxer
- PATCH, the floor manager rushdown
- BRUNO "THE FRIDGE", an armored grappler
- THE GREAT ZAMBINI, a teleporting card-throwing zoner
- OFFICER KRANE, a charge fighter with a riot shield
- LOTUS LIU, a drunken-stance fighter
- BONEYARD, the butcher of Block Street
- SPIN, an aerial b-boy
- GAZZA, who fights with a football that rebounds off the ring wall
- RERUN, the contestant who counters everything
- THE FREAK (mini boss) and RICKY MARQUEE, the host and final boss, who changes his act halfway through the fight. Clear THE SEASON to unlock both.

MODES:
- THE SEASON: an arcade ladder of 8 episodes against the CPU - random contestants, your rival, the mini boss and the host in his own control room. The CPU sidesteps straight attacks it reads, answers steppers with homing moves and circles off the wall. Two bonus rounds break it up: BRAWL BREAK (45 seconds against waves of studio goons that come at you from every side of the ring) after episode 3 and HECKLER TOSS (40 seconds of parrying what the crowd throws in from all around) after episode 6. Continues, a closing story for every contestant and a local score board. THE PILOT is the short cut: 5 episodes with BRAWL BREAK after episode 2.
- VERSUS: two players on one screen, or you against the CPU at difficulty 1 to 8, in any of the five arenas.
- ONLINE: quick match or a private four-letter room code, with rollback netcode.
- TRAINING: a dummy that stands, crouches, jumps, blocks, sidesteps, circles or fights back as a CPU, 3-second record and playback, input display, frame data, 3D hitboxes and every move list.

FIVE 360-DEGREE ARENAS, with the crowd on every side: The Rust Theater (a round pit with a blue brick wall), Butcher Block (an eight-sided ring of white tile), Wheel of Pain (a round ring of neon panels), Channel 13 Rooftop (a round ring of steel cables) and The Control Room (an eight-sided ring of steel rails).

Two control types with the same timing underneath: SIMPLE (the special button plus a direction) and CLASSIC (motion inputs). Keyboard, gamepad and on-screen touch controls (with two STEP buttons).

Comic violence only: hits land with a hard freeze and a red cartoon splash (or sparks, or confetti), never realistic gore.
sub_genre: 3D arena fighter (360-degree ring, sidestep and circle-walk)
controls_keyboard: P1: W A S D move, jump (W or SPACE) and crouch; hold back to block · Q / E step in / step out (tap = sidestep, hold = circle-walk around the opponent) · J light · K medium · L heavy · I special · U assist (hold) · H throw · O parry · P impact · Y taunt · ESC pause. P2 on the same keyboard: arrow keys · Numpad 7 / 9 step in / out · Numpad 1 / 2 / 3 light / medium / heavy · Numpad 5 special · Numpad 4 assist · Numpad 0 throw · Numpad 6 parry · Numpad + impact · Numpad * taunt
controls_gamepad: Standard gamepad: left stick or d-pad move · right stick up / down step in / step out (tap = sidestep, hold = circle-walk) · X light · Y medium · RB heavy · A special · B assist (hold) · LT throw · LB parry · RT impact · SELECT taunt · START pause
art_direction: Key art for a late-night TV fight show, built as stylised 3D with cel-shaded characters and thick ink outlines. Two fighters square off inside a round fighting pit, seen from a low three-quarter angle: a lean boxer in taped fists and a sleeveless shirt throwing a straight right, and a huge slab of a grappler with a shaved head, arms wide, ready to grab. A curved waist-high wall of blue-painted brick rings them, a shadowy crowd packs the tiers behind it all the way around, harsh studio spotlights from above, light haze. A red LIVE bug and a slanted yellow ratings frame suggest the broadcast without readable text. Saturated palette: ink purple-black #140d1f, signal red #ff2e4d, marquee yellow #ffd23a, cream #fff4e0. Punchy, comic energy with a motion-smear on the swing and a small cartoon impact star; no gore. No text, no logos, no ships, no pirates, no nautical props.
